wallet.body: Every delivered message is charged to your wallet at the price for its country and category. Failed messages are not charged.
wallet.funded: When the balance is empty, bulk sends are paused until you add money.

plan.allowance: Your plan includes {limit} messages every month.

kpi.costHint: Flat price when per-country pricing is off

economics.title: Economics
economics.flatPriceHint: At least 0.01. Use the rate grid for free messages.
economics.referralSignupHint: Paid to a referrer on the referee's first paid order.
economics.lowBalanceHint: Workspaces at or under this balance are warned.
economics.coverageHint: A bulk send is refused unless the wallet covers this share of its estimated cost. 0 refuses only an empty wallet.
economics.rewardSentence: A reward of {reward} pays for {count, plural, one {# message} other {# messages}} at the flat price.

problems.invalid: Enter an amount with at most 2 decimals.
problems.percent: Enter a whole number from 0 to 100.

perCountryEnabled.label: Per-country pricing
perCountryEnabled.on: On: each message is charged by the recipient's country and category from the rate card.
perCountryEnabled.off: Off: every message is charged the flat price.
perCountryEnabled.confirmOn: Messages will be charged by country and category from the next send.
perCountryEnabled.confirmOff: Messages will be charged the flat price from the next send.

payPerMessage.label: Charge per message
payPerMessage.on: On: workspaces without a plan allowance pay for each delivered message from their wallet.
payPerMessage.off: Off: messages are not charged to wallets.
payPerMessage.confirmOn: Delivered messages will be charged to wallets from now on.
payPerMessage.confirmOff: Wallets will no longer be charged for messages. This affects every workspace.

grid.title: Rate card
grid.modeOn: Per-country pricing is on: these prices are used.
grid.modeOff: Per-country pricing is off: these prices are saved but the flat price is charged.
grid.empty: No rates yet. Add a row, import a rate card or re-seed the starter card.
grid.removeBody: The rate for {country} is deleted. Messages fall back to the next matching rate.
grid.saved: {count, plural, one {# rate saved.} other {# rates saved.}}
grid.savedSome: {saved} saved, {skipped} skipped. See the reason on each skipped row.
grid.unsaved: {count, plural, one {# unsaved row} other {# unsaved rows}}
grid.tooMany: Too many changed rows for one save. Save in smaller batches.

problems.price: Enter a price with at most 2 decimals.
problems.metaCost: Enter a cost with at most 6 decimals.
problems.country: Use a 2-letter country code, or leave it blank for any country.
problems.empty: Enter a price or a Meta cost.
problems.duplicate: This country and category already has a row.

sync.title: Sync Meta costs
sync.untouched: Your prices are not changed. Only the cost Meta charges you is updated.
sync.bundledNote: No live Meta price list is connected, so the bundled rate card is used.

import.title: Import rate card
import.intro: Upload a CSV rate card. You see what would change before anything is saved.

fileProblems.tooBig: The file is larger than 4 MB.
fileProblems.unreadable: The file could not be read.

import.done: Rate card imported: {added} added, {updated} updated, {skipped} skipped.

seed.title: Re-seed the starter rate card?
seed.warning: This writes the bundled starter prices over existing rows for the same country and category. Prices you set by hand for those rows are replaced.
seed.done: {count, plural, one {# rate} other {# rates}} written from the starter card.

crossBorder.title: Cross-border sends
crossBorder.body: The price follows the recipient's country, not the workspace's. Add a row for every country you send to.

how.title: How a price is found
how.body: The wallet looks up the recipient's country and the message category in this card. A blank category or country matches anything.

order.title: Which row wins
order.body: An exact country and category match is used first, then the country with any category, then any country, then the flat price.

mode.title: How customers are priced
mode.intro: Choose what a message costs your customers. This applies to every workspace and is saved on its own.

fixed.label: Fixed prices
fixed.body: You type a price for each country and category in the rate card below. Margins are saved but not used.

margin.label: Meta cost + margin
margin.body: The customer pays Meta's cost plus your margin, set per country and category. Where Meta's cost is not known, the typed fixed price is charged.

mode.confirmFixed: Every workspace will be charged the fixed prices from the rate card from the next message. Margins stay saved but stop applying.
mode.confirmMargin: Every workspace will be charged Meta's cost plus the margin that applies to it (workspace override, then its plan, then the platform default) from the next message. Where Meta's cost is unknown, the fixed price is still charged.
mode.savedFixed: Customers are now priced with fixed prices.
mode.savedMargin: Customers are now priced with Meta cost plus margin.

metaCards.title: Meta rate cards
metaCards.intro: Meta publishes one price list for each currency, and changes it only on 1 January, 1 April, 1 July and 1 October. A workspace billed in INR is priced from Meta's INR list and charged to its INR wallet, never from the USD list converted. Import each file as Meta publishes it. Typed prices and the flat price are kept in the platform currency and converted at the exchange rate on file for a workspace billed in another currency.
metaCards.none: No Meta rate card is stored yet. Import the file Meta publishes for your currency.
metaCards.usedPricing: Pricing, margins and the reseller P&L, and workspaces billed in the platform currency

reminder.current: Up to date. Meta may next change its prices on {date}.
reminder.dueTitle: A new quarter began on {date}: Meta may have changed its prices.
reminder.dueBody: Download the new rate files (one per currency in use) and import them here. Until then, costs and margins use the older card.
reminder.upcomingTitle: Meta may change its prices on {date} ({days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} away).
reminder.upcomingBody: Have the new files ready to import that day.
reminder.missingBody: Workspaces set to that currency have no Meta price list to show. Import the file Meta publishes for it.

table.heading: Meta’s {currency} card
table.note: List price per delivered message, as Meta publishes it. Countries Meta does not name are priced as Other.

import.title: Import Meta rate card
import.intro: Choose the file Meta publishes for one currency (an Excel workbook, even where the link says CSV). The currency and effective date are read from the file. You see what would change before anything is saved.
import.hint: One currency per file. A new file replaces that currency’s card as a whole. At most 2 MB.

fileProblems.wrongType: Choose the .xlsx file Meta publishes, or a CSV saved from it.
fileProblems.tooBig: The file is larger than 2 MB, which is not a Meta rate card.
fileProblems.unreadable: The file could not be read.

import.appliesToPricing: This is the {currency} card, your platform currency. Importing it also refreshes the Meta cost behind pricing, margins and the reseller P&L ({added} new, {updated} updated). Customer prices are not changed.
import.storedOnly: This is not the platform currency. It is stored and shown, and it prices every workspace billed in {currency}. The Meta cost in the rate grid below stays in the platform currency.

workspaces.emptyBody: Change the search or clear the low-balance filter.

pricing.empty: No overrides. This workspace follows its plan and the platform default.

billingCurrency.title: Billing currency
billingCurrency.intro: Messages are priced from Meta's rate card for this currency and charged to the workspace's wallet in it. Top-ups are entered and credited in it too.
billingCurrency.notUsed: Not used for billing; the money stays here.

dialog.title: Change billing currency
dialog.effect: From now on messages are priced from Meta's {to} card and charged to the {to} wallet. Nothing is converted: the {from} wallet keeps its balance.
dialog.left: {amount} stays in the {from} wallet and is not used until the workspace is switched back.
dialog.reasonHint: Shown in the audit trail and the workspace's wallet log. At least 5 characters.

adjust.title: Adjust balance
adjust.reasonHint: Required, 5 to 500 characters. The workspace sees this reason on its statement.
adjust.cappedWarning: This is more than the balance of {balance}. Only what is there is deducted; the balance stops at 0.
adjust.visibleNote: The reason is shown to the workspace and kept in the audit log.

amount.invalid: Enter a positive amount with at most 2 decimals.
amount.zero: The amount must be greater than 0.
amount.tooLarge: That is above the limit for a single adjustment.

note.short: Say why in at least {min} characters.

logs.title: Wallet logs

margins.subtitle: What customers pay on top of Meta's cost, per country and message category.
margins.ratesFailed: Meta's costs could not be loaded, so prices for new rows cannot be shown.

mode.switchLink: Go to the pricing mode switch

scope.hint: The platform default applies to every plan. A plan's own margin beats it.

grid.unknownCost: Meta's cost is not known here, so the typed fixed price applies.

grid.removedPending: Will be removed when you save.

grid.unsaved: {count, plural, one {# unsaved row} other {# unsaved rows}}
grid.tooMany: Too many changed rows for one save. Save in smaller batches.

problems.margin: Enter a percentage from -100 to 1000 with at most 2 decimals. -100 means free.
problems.duplicate: This country and category already has a row.

layers.title: Which margin wins
layers.body: A workspace override beats its plan's margin, which beats the platform default. A layer is read in full before the next one.

specific.title: Most specific first
specific.body: Inside a layer, country and category is used first, then the country with any category, then the category in any country, then the default row.

unknown.title: When Meta's cost is unknown
unknown.body: The price is Meta's cost plus the margin, rounded to the nearest 0.01 and at least 0.01 unless the margin is -100% (free). Where Meta's cost is unknown, the typed fixed price applies instead.

packages.title: Credit packages
packages.subtitle: Optional offers: pay this much, get this much wallet credit. A credit above the price is a top-up bonus.
packages.deleteBody: Delete this package? Existing purchases keep their ledger rows.

empty.title: No credit packages yet
empty.bodyWrite: Create the first package to offer a wallet top-up with a bonus.
